item.text: I’m reviewing the current split between API, solver, CLI, and tests to find the next refactor that improves cohesion rather than just increasing file count. After that I’ll make one focused structural change and re-run the verification path.

The remaining useful refactor is to centralize the input contract. Right now validation, trivial-result handling, and sequence normalization are split between the public API and the solver constructor. I’m moving that into a dedicated request object so each layer has one responsibility: API delegates, request owns preconditions/normalization, solver only does DP.

The responsibilities are cleaner now: `LongestCommonSubsequence` is just the facade, `LcsRequest` owns the input contract and normalization, and `LcsSolver` only performs the DP pass. I’m compiling the full set and running the CLI plus tests to confirm behavior stayed stable.

I refactored the codebase by introducing [LcsRequest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/020_longest_common_subsequence/LcsRequest.java). That centralizes null checks, trivial-result fast paths, and sequence normalization in one place, instead of splitting those concerns between [LongestCommonSubsequence.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/020_longest_common_subsequence/LongestCommonSubsequence.java) and [LcsSolver.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/020_longest_common_subsequence/LcsSolver.java). The facade now delegates cleanly, and the solver only handles the DP algorithm.

Verification: `javac LongestCommonSubsequence.java LcsRequest.java LcsSolver.java LongestCommonSubsequenceCli.java LongestCommonSubsequenceTest.java` succeeded, `java LongestCommonSubsequenceTest` prints `All tests passed.`, and `java LongestCommonSubsequenceCli abc ace` prints `2`.
